meeting_header:
Date: 2025-07-22 14:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Murphy (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (FinNova PM), Jorge Alvarez (FinNova ML), Lena Park (FinNova Platform)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Murphy: okay um hey everyone thanks for joining the weekly caching sync, we are at 14:00 PT, quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya Singh: hey Priya here, Jorge and Lena are on as well.
[00:11] Jorge Alvarez: yep hey all, Jorge.
[00:13] Lena Park: Lena, hi.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood, ready to go.
[00:18] Alex Murphy: cool, agenda: quick recap of last week's run, prefix vs KV cache hit rates, prompt reuse strategy, proposed TTLs, and next steps. we'll try to keep it tight.
[00:31] Priya Singh: sounds good, we've got a packed week.
[00:34] Alex Murphy: Samir you wanna kick off with numbers from the 48 hour run?
[00:38] Samir Patel: yeah uh sure. so the run we did Wed to Fri, we instrumented prefix cache and KV cache separately. high level: overall token cost reduction about 22% compared to baseline without caching, latency p50 remained steady, p95 improved for repeated prefixes. specifically prefix cache hit rate for the login/account flows was ~46%, and KV cache hit rate for conversational context items around 28%. those are across both production-ish and synthetic traffic.
[01:10] Jorge Alvarez: hmm 28% KV seems lower than I expected. is that because KV keys are per-user?
[01:15] Samir Patel: good call. partly yes — currently our keying strategy uses the full convo id + turn id which fragments. when we normalize keys to conversational template + user bucket we expect hit rate to jump. also a lot of your prompts have small variations like timestamps, so prefix reuse is impacted.
[01:31] Priya Singh: the timestamps are usually in the system prompt, so if we strip or canonicalize them that should help. we can work on that.
[01:36] Lena Park: question on measurement: how confident are you in the hit rate numbers? i saw some spikes in the dashboard that looked off.
[01:43] Samir Patel: transcription note — the instrumentation is via our tracing hooks and token tags, it's medium confidence; there was some noise from parallel requests being counted twice in a small window, so margin +/- 3-5%. we flagged outliers and removed them.
[01:57] Alex Murphy: can you share the sheet again Samir? the one with per-route hit rates?
[02:01] Samir Patel: yup, link in chat — "POC_cache_results_20250722.xlsx". quick callouts: the onboarding flow has best prefix reuse (~61%) because it's templatized, while the billing inquiries have lots of free-form text and show only ~12% prefix hits.
[02:22] Jorge Alvarez: for KV are you storing embeddings or raw strings?
[02:25] Samir Patel: currently raw response fragments and some hashed prompt fingerprints. we can add a secondary embedding-based lookup for semantically similar prompts but that increases compute.
[02:35] Priya Singh: would embedding lookup make sense for our fuzzy billing questions?
[02:39] Samir Patel: yes, it could. trade-off is extra CPU during lookup vs higher hit rate. we estimate embedding precompute + ANN index could bump effective hit rate by 10-15% on that profile.
[02:50] Alex Murphy: Juliet from FinNova's infra asked offline about TTLs and memory pressure — what's the current TTL configuration used in the test?
[02:58] Samir Patel: we used conservative 30 minute TTL for prefix cache and 2 hour for KV cache in the first run. memory usage peaked but stayed under the Dedicated pilot cap; the eviction rate for students... i mean, for entries was about 6% per hour during peak traffic.
[03:18] Priya Singh: ok 30 minutes prefix seems short for some repeated flows, like support threads that recur within a day.
[03:24] Samir Patel: agreed, for those we propose staged TTLs: short tail 15m for ephemeral prompts, 2h for session-level patterns, and 24h for rare but stable templates like onboarding. we can also tier by route.
[03:38] Jorge Alvarez: would that increase our memory footprint drastically?
[03:41] Samir Patel: depends on route cardinality. onboarding route has low cardinality so 24h is cheap. billing is high cardinality so we'd keep it lower or use hashed buckets. also can enable LFU eviction to keep the most useful entries.
[03:53] Lena Park: LFU sounds good. can we get a simulation of memory vs TTL tradeoffs?
[03:58] Samir Patel: yes, next step we can run a 24 hour sim on your actual traffic sample to show hit rates, memory, and cost. that's in the action items.
[04:08] Alex Murphy: great. quick question from security angle — Priya tagged that they need KMS integration for cache encryption at rest. we have customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated, right?
[04:19] Samir Patel: yes, Dedicated supports KMS/HSM for cache encryption; in Private you manage keys directly. for hosted we do server-side encryption but we can do envelope encryption integrations for enterprise.
[04:30] Priya Singh: for the pilot we'd prefer Dedicated with KMS if cost works. can you put that in the estimate?
[04:36] Alex Murphy: will do. i'll add Dedicated + cache uplift line items.
[04:39] Jorge Alvarez: another technical: when the cache misses and we fall back to the larger model, is there a way to async populate the KV so the next request benefits?
[04:48] Samir Patel: yes, async population on miss is supported — background writeback option. the trade-off is extra write I/O and potential consistency lag; but it boosts subsequent hit rates. we recommend it for high-value routes.
[05:01] Priya Singh: how about prompt canonicalization — we talked about removing timestamps. who owns that work on our side?
[05:07] Jorge Alvarez: I can own creating a canonicalizer for billing prompts — strip timestamps, normalize currency, reduce synonyms. will take me a few days.
[05:14] Alex Murphy: put that as an action item.
[05:16] Samir Patel: quick note — canonicalization can also be done at the frontend or as a lightweight middleware in your API layer, whichever is easiest.
[05:25] Priya Singh: we'll likely do middleware. less invasive.
[05:29] Alex Murphy: ok moving on to prompt reuse strategy — we did a small experiment with template-driven prompts and saw a 2.3x prefix hit rate for those routes.
[05:39] Jorge Alvarez: what's the effort to convert more prompts to templates?
[05:43] Samir Patel: it's mostly product work: identify common intents, create placeholders for variables, and enforce schema. for FinNova's top 10 intents it should be 1-2 weeks of PM+engineering.
[05:54] Priya Singh: we can prioritize top 5 first.
[05:57] Alex Murphy: timeline-wise, if we canonicalize and template top 5 by next week and we run Samir's 24h sim over weekend, we should have updated hit rates by Monday. feasible?
[06:07] Jorge Alvarez: yes I can push that.
[06:09] Samir Patel: note: for the sim we need the prompt set and representative traffic, Jorge if you can upload to the shared S3 by Thursday EOD we'll schedule the run Friday.
[06:19] Jorge Alvarez: will do.
[06:20] Alex Murphy: excellent. another topic — cold start behavior when a new user or new template appears, how much does latency spike?
[06:28] Samir Patel: cold starts are mostly due to kernel warmup and KV lookups triggering DB reads. p95 latency can move from 420ms to ~1.1s for the first few requests for that key. with async prepopulation or predictive caching (proactive fill based on events) we can reduce that.
[06:46] Priya Singh: predictive fill sounds interesting, what's the cost?
[06:50] Samir Patel: depends on traffic volume and prediction accuracy; rough estimate is 5-12% extra token cost to save p95 tails for targeted routes.
[06:59] Lena Park: for SLAs we care about p95 more than average cost. we might accept some cost to protect latency.
[07:05] Alex Murphy: makes sense. combine predictive fill only for session-authenticated flows where value is higher.
[07:13] Priya Singh: on the UI side we can mark certain routes as low-latency critical.
[07:17] Samir Patel: nice. i'll add route tagging to config so the optimizer treats them differently.
[07:22] Alex Murphy: anything else on measurements?
[07:25] Jorge Alvarez: curious about hit eviction patterns — can you show LFU vs LRU in the next dashboard?
[07:30] Samir Patel: yes, we have both metrics; will add a comparison chart.
[07:34] Priya Singh: can you also include cost per 1k tokens with caching vs without?
[07:38] Samir Patel: yep that's in the sheet.
[07:40] Alex Murphy: quick interruption — Marta just joined, she's on security. Marta, do you want to say hi?
[07:45] Marta: hi all, sorry for the delay. I'm Marta from FinNova security. couple quick Qs: audit logs for cache access, and retention of cached items — are those logged?
[07:56] Samir Patel: yes, cache access logs can be routed to your SIEM; we log reads/writes with token-level metadata for Dedicated and Private. TTLs are configurable per route and we'll include retention policy in the security doc.
[08:08] Marta: great, also we need to see encryption at rest details.
[08:11] Alex Murphy: Alex will send the SOC2 excerpt and the KMS integration page.
[08:16] Marta: thanks.
[08:18] Alex Murphy: circling back: we recommended three experiments — 1) canonicalize prompts for top 5 intents, 2) run 24h TTL sweep sim with actual traffic, 3) try embedding-based KV lookup for billing intents. prioritize 1 & 2.
[08:33] Priya Singh: agree.
[08:34] Jorge Alvarez: timeline wise i can drop canonicalized prompts by Thursday and upload traffic sample, Samir runs sim Friday, results Monday.
[08:41] Samir Patel: yep i'll schedule. and on the embedding option we'll prototype next week and present trade-offs.
[08:49] Alex Murphy: ok excellent. any blockers?
[08:52] Lena Park: only scheduling peering window for Dedicated — i'll confirm dates.
[08:57] Alex Murphy: action items recap: Samir run sim and slide deck, Jorge upload prompt set, Alex share pricing and security docs, Lena confirm peering. we'll also update the sheet with LFU/LRU comparison.
[09:12] Priya Singh: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:14] Alex Murphy: thanks, see you next week.
[09:16] [end of meeting]
